title: China's Water Towns Are 1,300 Years Old — Streets Made of Water | China Travel Expert
description:
China has canal towns more than 1,300 years old — where the streets are water and the boats are the taxis.

In the Jiangnan region south of the Yangtze, towns like Wuzhen (over 1,300 years of history) and Zhouzhuang (first built in 1086, more than 900 years old) grew up along a web of canals. Stone arch bridges cross the water, wooden houses lean out over it, and cars still can't reach many of the front doors. Several of these ancient waterfront towns sit on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list.

🧭 Expert Tip: Reach Wuzhen or Zhouzhuang right at dawn — the canals are mirror-still and the day-trip crowds haven't arrived yet.
